name: Ammiel
overview: Ammiel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically as the sixth-born son of Obed-edom. His identity is primarily grounded in his Levitical heritage and his position within his family, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:4. No additional personal notes or attributes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Ammiel means 'G-d [El] is my kinsman,' reflecting a personal relationship or connection to God. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological significance as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:5.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ammiel as the son of Obed-edom, establishing his place within a Levitical family line. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Ammiel's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his lineage as a Levite and as a descendant of Obed-edom, who is known for his service related to the Ark of the Covenant. While the text does not elaborate on Ammiel's individual actions, his inclusion highlights the importance of Levitical families in the worship and service of God during the period chronicled in 1 Chronicles.
